title: BUN–albumin interaction does not establish improved maximum-grip prediction across two NHANES cycles
abstract: A centered serum blood-urea-nitrogen (BUN) by albumin interaction was tested beyond flexible individual laboratory measurements, BUN/creatinine and BUN/albumin ratios, anthropometry and demographics. Weighted ridge models trained in4055 NHANES2011–2012 adults were transferred without target fitting to4581 separately sampled2013–2014 adults. Target MSE changed35.294982→35.325237kg²; baseline-minus-augmented gain was−0.030254kg² (conditional target-PSU95% interval[−0.139318,0.077493]; full-source-preprocessing and source-target-PSU refit interval[−0.263522,0.166817]). Penalty, sex and reference-range sensitivities changed direction. Source PSU-grouped CV weakly favored augmentation but confirmation did not. This scoped negative test does not establish equivalence, clinical utility or a catabolic mechanism.
